h1: UPS vs Solar vs Generator: Cost per Backup Hour Over Five Years
author: ali-ahmad

answer: For {{in.load_w|int}} W through {{in.hours|int}} hours of loadshedding a day, the cheapest backup over {{in.years|int}} years is {{out.cheapest|raw}}: about {{out.solar_per_hour|rs}} per backup hour, against {{out.ups_per_hour|rs}} for a UPS with tubular batteries and {{out.gen_per_hour|rs}} for a petrol generator. Total cost = equipment + running cost each year + battery replacements, divided by the hours of backup.
how: Backup a day: {{out.load_w}} W × {{out.hours}} h = {{out.day_kwh|2}} kWh; backup hours: {{out.hours}} h × {{out.days}} days × twelve months × {{out.years}} years = {{out.backup_hours|int}} h. UPS: {{out.ups_kva}} kVA, tubular batteries: {{out.batteries|int}} ({{out.bank_wh|int}} Wh needed), {{out.ups_buy|rs}}; recharge {{out.recharge_kwh_year|int}} units a year × {{out.tariff|rs2}} = {{out.ups_run_year|rs}}; {{out.ups_repl|int}} battery replacements {{out.ups_repl_rs|rs}}; total {{out.ups_total|rs}} ÷ {{out.backup_hours|int}} h = {{out.ups_per_hour|rs}}. Generator: {{out.gen_kva}} kVA, {{out.gen_buy|rs}}; {{out.l_per_h|2}} litres an hour × {{out.run_h_year|int}} h × {{out.fuel_price|rs2}} = {{out.fuel_year|rs}} fuel plus {{out.oil_year|rs}} oil a year; total {{out.gen_total|rs}} ÷ {{out.backup_hours|int}} h = {{out.gen_per_hour|rs}}. Hybrid solar: {{out.inverter_kw}} kW inverter, {{out.lithium_packs|int}} lithium pack(s), {{out.panels|int}} panels, {{out.solar_buy|rs}}; {{out.solar_repl|int}} battery replacements {{out.solar_repl_rs|rs}}; total {{out.solar_total|rs}} ÷ {{out.backup_hours|int}} h = {{out.solar_per_hour|rs}}.
key_facts: Cost per backup hour = (equipment + running cost a year × years + battery replacements) ÷ hours of backup over the same years; it puts a cheap-to-buy generator and a dear-to-buy solar system on one scale.

For {{in.load_w|int}} W through {{in.hours|int}} hours a day a petrol generator burns about {{out.l_per_h|2}} litres an hour, {{out.fuel_year|rs}} of petrol a year, so it is the dearest option within the first year even though it is the cheapest to buy.

A UPS takes more units from the grid than it delivers: {{out.recharge_kwh_year|int}} units a year here, {{out.ups_run_year|rs}} at {{out.tariff|rs2}} a unit, and its tubular batteries are replaced every {{out.tubular_life_years|int}} years.

For a small load and short cuts the UPS wins: {{ex.1.in.load_w|int}} W for {{ex.1.in.hours|int}} hours a day costs {{ex.1.out.ups_per_hour|rs}} per backup hour on a UPS against {{ex.1.out.solar_per_hour|rs}} on hybrid solar, because even a small solar backup buys a whole lithium pack and a hybrid inverter.

formula.text: Cost per backup hour = (B + Y × R + N × P) ÷ (h × days × twelve × Y)
lines: B = equipment price (middle of the price range in our data, installation extra); Y = years compared
R = running cost a year: UPS recharge units × tariff; generator fuel (litres an hour × hours × price) + oil changes; hybrid solar none
N × P = battery replacements within the period × battery price (none in the final year of life)
Battery bank: UPS tubular Wh = load W × h ÷ (DoD × inverter efficiency); lithium kWh likewise, bought in whole packs
Generator litres an hour = no-load fuel × rated kW + fuel per kWh × load kW (the fuel calculator's curve)

sections.h2: Which is the cheapest backup for loadshedding?
p: With the defaults, {{in.load_w|int}} W for {{in.hours|int}} hours a day over {{in.years|int}} years, the answer is {{out.cheapest|raw}}. Its total is {{out.solar_total|rs}} against {{out.ups_total|rs}} for the UPS and {{out.gen_total|rs}} for the generator, because it has no running cost once bought.

The answer changes with the load and the hours. For {{ex.1.in.load_w|int}} W over {{ex.1.in.hours|int}} hours a day the UPS is cheapest ({{ex.1.out.ups_total|rs}} over five years), because hybrid solar still has to buy a whole lithium pack and an inverter. Enter your own load and hours above.

A petrol generator runs its engine for every hour of backup, and even lightly loaded it burns a large share of its full-load fuel. At {{out.fuel_price|rs2}} a litre that is {{out.fuel_year|rs}} a year here, plus {{out.oil_year|rs}} of engine oil at one change every {{out.oil_change_hours|int}} running hours.

A UPS only pays for the units it takes back from the grid, which are more than it delivers because of charger and inverter losses: {{out.recharge_kwh_year|int}} units, {{out.ups_run_year|rs}} a year. Its real cost is the batteries, replaced every {{out.tubular_life_years|int}} years.

sections.h2: What the hybrid solar figure includes
p: The smallest hybrid inverter in our price data that carries the load, lithium batteries in whole packs for one night's backup, and enough panels to refill the battery on an average day in your city. It assumes the sun recharges the battery, so a run of cloudy days would still need the grid.
It does not count the bill savings solar makes during the day, which usually decide the choice in its favour, nor mounting, cabling and installation, which add to every option but most to solar.

Every figure is the middle of a price range from Pakistani retailer listings or our solar price tracker, equipment only, each listed under Sources with its publisher. Retailer prices for the same model differ a lot, so replace them with your own quotes before you decide.
Battery lives are planning values: tubular {{out.tubular_life_years|int}} years and lithium {{out.lifepo4_life_years|int}} years. Heat, deep discharges and poor charging shorten both.

mistakes: Comparing purchase prices only. The generator is cheapest to buy and dearest to own; compare the cost per backup hour over the same years.
Forgetting battery replacements. A tubular bank is replaced every few years, which can cost as much as the UPS and the first batteries together.
Sizing the comparison on the whole house. Backup usually runs fans, lights and a few appliances; enter only what runs during a cut.
Treating the solar total as a backup cost alone. Hybrid solar also cuts the day bill, which this comparison leaves out, so it is the most conservative figure for solar.
safety: A generator needs a proper changeover switch so it can never feed the grid, and must run outdoors away from windows; a UPS or hybrid inverter connects to the house wiring at mains voltage. Have a licensed electrician fit the changeover, the inverter and the earthing for whichever option you choose.

faq.q: Which is cheaper for loadshedding: UPS, solar or generator?
faq.a: It depends on the load and the hours. For {{in.load_w|int}} W through {{in.hours|int}} hours a day over {{in.years|int}} years, {{out.cheapest|raw}} is cheapest at {{out.solar_per_hour|rs}} per backup hour; for {{ex.1.in.load_w|int}} W through {{ex.1.in.hours|int}} hours a UPS is cheapest at {{ex.1.out.ups_per_hour|rs}}.

faq.q: How much does a petrol generator cost per hour?
faq.a: For {{in.load_w|int}} W on a {{out.gen_kva}} kVA set, about {{out.l_per_h|2}} litres an hour, {{out.fuel_year|rs}} of petrol a year at {{in.hours|int}} hours a day, plus oil. With the purchase spread over {{in.years|int}} years that is {{out.gen_per_hour|rs}} per backup hour.

faq.q: How much does it cost to recharge a UPS battery?
faq.a: The units a UPS takes from the grid are its backup units divided by the charger and inverter efficiencies: {{out.recharge_kwh_year|int}} units a year for the default load, {{out.ups_run_year|rs}} at {{out.tariff|rs2}} a unit.

faq.q: How long do UPS batteries last in Pakistan?
faq.a: Tubular batteries usually last two to five years in Pakistani heat; this calculator uses {{out.tubular_life_years|int}} years. Lithium (LiFePO4) packs are rated for thousands of cycles; it uses {{out.lifepo4_life_years|int}} years.

faq.q: Is solar worth it only for backup?
faq.a: For a small load and short cuts, usually not: a whole lithium pack and a hybrid inverter cost more than a UPS. For bigger loads and long cuts it is the cheapest per backup hour even before counting its daytime bill savings.
No. All three use equipment prices only. Installation, wiring and a changeover switch add to each, most to solar.
